channel.title: DOX
channel.description: News and releases of Dox, the web backend framework for Dart.

item.author: Dox team

item.author: Dox team
item.description: This release has a security fix for the native HTTP server and for the native HTTP client. We recommend that you update. The server also has 10 more fixes...

item.title: Live updates with Socket.IO in Dox
item.author: Dox team
item.description: This post shows how to add live updates to a Dox app with Socket.IO. When one user changes data, the screens of the other users change too, with no refresh.

item.title: Isolate groups: each isolate gets its own memory
item.author: Dox team
item.description: Dox can now give each server isolate its own heap and its own garbage collector. One flag turns it on. In our test, the same app did 9% more requests a...

item.title: HTTPS without a proxy in Dox
item.author: Dox team
item.description: Dox can now serve HTTPS itself. Give it a certificate file and a key file, and a small server needs no proxy for TLS. HTTPS is off by default, so an app...

item.title: HTTP/2 and gRPC in Dox
item.author: Dox team
item.description: Dox now serves HTTP/2 and gRPC on the same port as your HTTP routes. HTTP/2 is off by default, so an app that does not turn it on works the same as before.

item.title: GraphQL in Dox
item.author: Dox team
item.description: The new dox_graphql package makes a GraphQL API for your app from your models. You add annotations to a model, run the builder, and the API is ready.

item.title: A full-stack app with Dox and Inertia
item.author: Dox team
item.description: This post shows how to build a React app on top of Dox with Inertia, with no separate API between them.

item.title: Dox vs Serverpod: which Dart backend fits your app
item.author: Dox team
item.description: Dox and Serverpod side by side: endpoints, models, ORM, migrations, background jobs, auth, mail and deploy, with code from each, so you can pick a Dart backend.

item.title: Dox vs Node.js: memory and speed
item.author: Dox team
item.description: In our published benchmark on 2 CPU cores, a Dox app served more requests per second than a Node.js app and used much less memory.

item.title: Dox vs Go: speed and memory
item.author: Dox team
item.description: In our published benchmark on 2 CPU cores, a Dox app handled 2× to 4.8× the requests per second of a Go app. Go used less memory once a database was added.

item.description: This post is a short tour of the parts that come with Dox, from routing and validation to the ORM, login, queues, mail and the CLI.

item.title: Deploy a Dart server to production with Dox
item.author: Dox team
item.description: How to deploy a Dart server to production with Dox: a native binary, a small Docker image, config from the env, HTTPS, a health check and a clean shutdown.
